def reputation_schedule(rep, contracts):
    """
    You run a mercenary company that starts with reputation `rep`.

    There are n available contracts; contracts[i] = [req_i, delta_i].
    You may execute each contract at most once, in any order you choose.
    You may execute contract i only when your current reputation is at
    least req_i, and executing it changes your reputation by delta_i
    (delta_i may be negative).  Your reputation must remain >= 0 at all
    times (in particular, immediately after every contract).

    For every k in 0..n, determine the maximum reputation you can end
    with after executing EXACTLY k contracts, over all choices of k
    contracts and all execution orders.  If no k contracts can be
    executed in any order, the answer for that k is -1.

    Input domain:
        0 <= rep <= 10**9
        0 <= n <= 200, contracts is a list of n pairs [req_i, delta_i]
        0 <= req_i <= 10**9,  -10**9 <= delta_i <= 10**9
        All values are ints.

    Returns:
        A list of n+1 ints; entry k is the answer for exactly k
        contracts (entry 0 is always rep).  Reputation 0 is a valid
        end state, so -1 unambiguously means "impossible".

    >>> reputation_schedule(3, [[0, 2], [4, -3], [5, 1]])
    [3, 5, 6, 3]
    >>> reputation_schedule(7, [[0, 4], [10, -2], [9, -4], [11, -6]])
    [7, 11, 9, 5, -1]
    >>> reputation_schedule(0, [[5, -1]])
    [0, -1]
    """
